SEN.note: Nothing on rules or authority for AI harms.
The supercomputer serves research; no government body is stated to use AI in administration.
Use cases named are genome sequencing and ocean and weather models, not AI tools in a public sector system.

facts.fact: CINERI director general Ousmane Thiare says the Taouey supercomputer is operational part-time, its second cell holding the GPU resources and often idled by power instability, while CPU resources are ready at full use.

Thiare says use of Taouey has been free and open to all since its arrival, with a webinar of over 200 online participants on 30 March 2026 and users named from UCAD's faculty of medicine and from environment and meteorology research.

SEN.note: Sovereignty is discussed in general terms; nothing on state data rules or hosting.
Only power instability at one site; no grid-wide outage count.
Startups are named as intended users only; no startup law or fund.
Nothing on hubs or technology parks.
